chapter.title: How we measure
chapter.subtitle: What to compare with, and how to count
chapter.sub: Chapter seven: how we measure. What do we compare a score with, and how do we count agreement?
chapter.tts: Chapter seven. How we measure. What do we compare a score with, and how do we count agreement?

lines.sub: We have our scores. But before we measure whether a score is right, we have to decide what to compare it with.
lines.tts: We have our scores. But before we measure whether a score is right, we have to decide what to compare it with.

lines.sub: Look at the ladder on the left: the higher the rung, the stricter the comparison.
lines.tts: Look at the ladder on the left. The higher the rung, the stricter the comparison.

lines.sub: Let's start at the bottom rung, the easiest comparison: proxies from the same window.
lines.tts: Let's start at the bottom rung, the easiest comparison, proxies from the same window.

lines.sub: A proxy is a simple stand-in measure.
lines.tts: A proxy is a simple stand-in measure.

lines.sub: But these proxies are computed from the very records the score was built from, so part of the agreement is to be expected.
lines.tts: But these proxies are computed from the very records the score was built from, so part of the agreement is to be expected.

lines.sub: That is why I do not call this validation.
lines.tts: That is why I do not call this validation.

lines.sub: I call it an intended-construct check.
lines.tts: I call it an intended-construct check.

lines.sub: The construct is what the score set out to measure, and the check asks whether the score really measures it.
lines.tts: The construct is what the score set out to measure, and the check asks whether the score really measures it.

lines.sub: See the little mirror icon: the score is, in a sense, looking at itself in a mirror.
lines.tts: See the little mirror icon. The score is, in a sense, looking at itself in a mirror.

lines.sub: One rung up is a stricter test: the out-of-window test.
lines.tts: One rung up is a stricter test, the out-of-window test.

lines.sub: It freezes the score and asks whether it predicts what happened afterwards.
lines.tts: It freezes the score and asks whether it predicts what happened afterwards.

lines.sub: The labels, the later outcomes we grade it against, are the new approval pairs and the new transfer senders.
lines.tts: The labels, the later outcomes we grade it against, are the new approval pairs and the new transfer senders.

lines.sub: The strictest rung, at the top, is an outcome that neither edge type contains.
lines.tts: The strictest rung, at the top, is an outcome that neither edge type contains.

lines.sub: Its icon shows the amber allowance arrow and the blue transfer arrow, both crossed out.
lines.tts: Its icon shows the amber allowance arrow and the blue transfer arrow, both crossed out.

lines.sub: In this study, that is the liquidation of contract traders on GMX V2, where a liquidation means a position closed by force.
lines.tts: In this study, that is the liquidation of contract traders on G M X V two, where a liquidation means a position closed by force.

lines.sub: The same-window check has three proxy families, listed on the right.
lines.tts: The same-window check has three proxy families, listed on the right.

lines.sub: The transfer family, in blue, uses transfer in-degree and in-value.
lines.tts: The transfer family, in blue, uses transfer in-degree and in-value.

lines.sub: The allowance family, in amber, uses in-approve degree and in-approve value, with the cap U.
lines.tts: The allowance family, in amber, uses in-approve degree and in-approve value, with the cap U.

lines.sub: Then comes the Sybil-stability family. A Sybil attack means creating many fake addresses to inflate a reputation.
lines.tts: Then comes the Sybil-stability family. A Sybil attack means creating many fake addresses to inflate a reputation.

lines.sub: This family looks at whether a contract traded over a long time, steadily and with many counterparties.
lines.tts: This family looks at whether a contract traded over a long time, steadily and with many counterparties.

lines.sub: It is a weak check, so no hypothesis rests on it.
lines.tts: It is a weak check, so no hypothesis rests on it.

lines.sub: How well a score agrees with later outcomes is measured with Kendall's τ.
lines.tts: How well a score agrees with later outcomes is measured with Kendall's tau.

card.title: Kendall's τ
card.body: Agreement of two rankings, counted pair by pair, from −1 to +1

lines.sub: Let me build a small example with five contracts.
lines.tts: Let me build a small example with five contracts.

lines.sub: In the top right, four counters start at 0.
lines.tts: In the top right, four counters start at zero.

lines.sub: Here are the five contracts. The amber bars are the scores, and the white bars are the outcome labels we grade them against later.
lines.tts: Here are the five contracts. The amber bars are the scores, and the white bars are the outcome labels we grade them against later.

lines.sub: First, let's count the pairs.
lines.tts: First, let's count the pairs.

lines.sub: Think of the contracts as people who each shake hands once with everyone else.
lines.tts: Think of the contracts as people who each shake hands once with everyone else.

lines.sub: Contract A shakes hands with the 4 others.
lines.tts: Contract A shakes hands with the four others.

lines.sub: All five shake 4 hands each, so 5 times 4 is 20.
lines.tts: All five shake four hands each, so five times four is twenty.

lines.sub: But contract A shaking hands with B, and B shaking hands with A, is the same handshake.
lines.tts: But contract A shaking hands with B, and B shaking hands with A, is the same handshake.

lines.sub: So we counted every handshake twice. Dividing by 2 gives 10.
lines.tts: So we counted every handshake twice. Dividing by two gives ten.

lines.sub: As a formula: n times (n − 1), all divided by 2, where n is the number of contracts.
lines.tts: As a formula, n times the quantity n minus one, all divided by two, where n is the number of contracts.

lines.sub: Now look at each pair.
lines.tts: Now look at each pair.

lines.sub: If the contract with the higher score also has the higher label, the pair is concordant, which means in agreement.
lines.tts: If the contract with the higher score also has the higher label, the pair is concordant, which means in agreement.

lines.sub: If it is the other way round, it is discordant.
lines.tts: If it is the other way round, it is discordant.

lines.sub: Take A and B. Contract A has the higher score, 5 against 4, but B has the higher label, 4 against 3.
lines.tts: Take A and B. Contract A has the higher score, five against four, but B has the higher label, four against three.

lines.sub: So they are discordant: the red line in the picture.
lines.tts: So they are discordant, the red line in the picture.

lines.sub: Contract A is concordant with C, with D and with E.
lines.tts: Contract A is concordant with C, with D and with E.

lines.sub: Counting the rest, there are 8 concordant pairs and 1 discordant pair.
lines.tts: Counting the rest, there are eight concordant pairs and one discordant pair.

lines.sub: C and D have the same label, so they count as neither. That is the dashed line.
lines.tts: C and D have the same label, so they count as neither. That is the dashed line.

lines.sub: Take the concordant pairs minus the discordant pairs and divide by all the pairs.
lines.tts: Take the concordant pairs minus the discordant pairs and divide by all the pairs.

lines.sub: 8 minus 1 is 7, and 7 over 10 gives 0.7.
lines.tts: Eight minus one is seven, and seven over ten gives zero point seven.

lines.sub: We write this as τ_a. It is the basic tau, which does not treat ties separately.
lines.tts: We write this as tau A. It is the basic tau, which does not treat ties separately.

lines.sub: On the scale below, 1 means the order is exactly the same, 0 means no relation, and −1 means exactly the opposite.
lines.tts: On the scale below, one means the order is exactly the same, zero means no relation, and minus one means exactly the opposite.

lines.sub: An aside: when there are no ties, 1 plus τ, all divided by 2, is the probability that a randomly chosen pair is in the same order in both rankings.
lines.tts: An aside. When there are no ties, one plus tau, all divided by two, is the probability that a randomly chosen pair is in the same order in both rankings.

lines.sub: In the actual matched cohort, there are 114,103,171 contract pairs, more than 110 million.
lines.tts: In the actual matched cohort, there are one hundred fourteen million one hundred three thousand one hundred seventy-one contract pairs, more than a hundred and ten million.

lines.sub: Back to C and D. A pair with the same label, a tie, is neither right nor wrong.
lines.tts: Back to C and D. A pair with the same label, a tie, is neither right nor wrong.

lines.sub: When there are many ties, the formula we just used cannot reach 1, however well the score predicts.
lines.tts: When there are many ties, the formula we just used cannot reach one, however well the score predicts.

lines.sub: So the divisor, the number we divide by, should keep only the truly ordered pairs, and three new counters keep track of the ties.
lines.tts: So the divisor, the number we divide by, should keep only the truly ordered pairs, and three new counters keep track of the ties.

lines.sub: Let's count the tied pairs first.
lines.tts: Let's count the tied pairs first.

lines.sub: A tie group of size 2 gives 1 pair, and a group of size 3 gives 3 pairs, just like the handshakes.
lines.tts: A tie group of size two gives one pair, and a group of size three gives three pairs, just like the handshakes.

lines.sub: So for a group of size t, we take t times (t − 1), all divided by 2.
lines.tts: So for a group of size t, we take t times the quantity t minus one, all divided by two.

lines.sub: In this example the scores have no ties, so n₁ is 0.
lines.tts: In this example the scores have no ties, so n one is zero.

lines.sub: The labels have one group, C and D, so n₂ is 1.
lines.tts: The labels have one group, C and D, so n two is one.

lines.sub: Take the tied pairs away from all 10: the score ranking puts 10 pairs in order, and the label ranking puts 9 in order.
lines.tts: Take the tied pairs away from all ten. The score ranking puts ten pairs in order, and the label ranking puts nine in order.

lines.sub: Instead of picking one of the two numbers, picture a rectangle 10 wide and 9 high, and take the square with the same area.
lines.tts: Instead of picking one of the two numbers, picture a rectangle ten wide and nine high, and take the square with the same area.

lines.sub: Its side is called the geometric mean: the square root of 90, about 9.487.
lines.tts: Its side is called the geometric mean, the square root of ninety, about nine point four eight seven.

lines.sub: So τ_b is 7 divided by 9.487, which is 0.738.
lines.tts: So tau b is seven divided by nine point four eight seven, which is zero point seven three eight.

card.title: τ_b
card.body: Kendall's τ corrected for ties; every τ in this thesis is τ_b

lines.sub: On the scale, it sits just above the τ_a of 0.7.
lines.tts: On the scale, it sits just above the tau A of zero point seven.

lines.sub: Without ties, n₁ and n₂ are 0, so τ_b equals the τ_a from before.
lines.tts: Without ties, n one and n two are zero, so tau b equals the tau A from before.

lines.sub: Every τ in this thesis is τ_b.
lines.tts: Every tau in this thesis is tau b.

lines.sub: The correction matters because plain counts and later labels are integers, and many contracts have zero, so there are a great many ties.
lines.tts: The correction matters because plain counts and later labels are integers, and many contracts have zero, so there are a great many ties.

lines.sub: We also report Spearman's ρ, shown in this aside.
lines.tts: We also report Spearman's rho, shown in this aside.

lines.sub: Put the ranks from the two rankings side by side: the smaller the rank differences, the closer the value is to 1.
lines.tts: Put the ranks from the two rankings side by side. The smaller the rank differences, the closer the value is to one.

lines.sub: In this example it is 0.872.
lines.tts: In this example it is zero point eight seven two.

lines.sub: C and D have the same label, so they share rank 2.5, halfway between 2nd and 3rd.
lines.tts: C and D have the same label, so they share rank two point five, halfway between second and third.

lines.sub: A more advanced note: without ties, ρ = 1 minus a fraction: 6 times the sum of the squared differences, over n times (n² − 1).
lines.tts: A more advanced note. Without ties, rho equals one minus a fraction. Six times the sum of the squared differences, over n times the quantity n squared minus one.

lines.sub: The 6 is a constant of the formula, and I skip its derivation.
lines.tts: The six is a constant of the formula, and I skip its derivation.

lines.sub: Here the squared differences add up to 2.5, so the formula gives 0.875.
lines.tts: Here the squared differences add up to two point five, so the formula gives zero point eight seven five.

lines.sub: But there are ties, so the thesis computes the correlation of the mid-ranks, the shared ranks like 2.5, and that value is 0.872.
lines.tts: But there are ties, so the thesis computes the correlation of the mid-ranks, the shared ranks like two point five, and that value is zero point eight seven two.

lines.sub: Spearman's ρ mostly tells the same story as τ.
lines.tts: Spearman's rho mostly tells the same story as tau.
